text:
Maya Chen: Quick heads-up — Luka from Acme flagged that several APAC trial accounts did not receive localized onboarding emails this morning (they got English instead of Japanese/Korean). Could be a translation fallback bug. Need comm plan for affected accounts.
Adrian Patel: Thanks, Maya. How many accounts impacted and which regions? Any immediate customer-visible failures besides the email language?
Maya Chen: Initial list is 8 accounts in JP/KR/AU timezones. Onboarding flows still work otherwise — they can log in and call the API — but they missed localized invite + scheduled office-hour link. Luka said a few customers assumed onboarding stalled.
Jules Rivera: Root cause: during yesterday's config swap we removed the legacy translation header mapping. New translate-v2 expects "Accept-Language" tokens; if absent we fall back to en-US. The outbound-email service wasn't sending Accept-Language on our queued messages, so localization fell back to English. Patch already identified.
incident-bot: Incident OP-2026-22 created for localization fallback (priority: P2).
Adrian Patel: Ok. We need a concise customer-safe update, mitigation steps, and a goodwill offer. Draft suggestion: "We discovered your onboarding email was sent in English due to a localization service regression. We’ve fixed the issue, resent the localized email, and booked a dedicated onboarding session in your timezone. We’ve also applied a $200 credit to your account. Apologies for the confusion." Thoughts?
Maya Chen: That wording is good. Add an ask for feedback and a way to escalate if they still see missing translations. Also propose sending the localized email immediately and confirming with recipients.
Jules Rivera: I'll run the resend job once we get approvals. Command to requeue localized messages (will only touch affected accounts):
```
./scripts/resend_localized_emails --accounts acme-42,zenlabs-7,nekko-3 --lang-detect accept-language
```
Action plan: 1) Approve customer message 2) Run resend job 3) Book 1:1 office hours (JP/KR CS) 4) Apply credit 5) Send follow-up survey in localized language in 72 hours.
Adrian Patel: Approving now. Maya, can you coordinate the email copy and timing? I'll sign off on credits and office hours. Jules, hold the job until Maya posts final copy.
Maya Chen: Draft email (subject + body snippet):
Subject: "Welcome — localized onboarding resources from Redwood"
Body snippet: "Hi {first_name}, we noticed your onboarding email was unintentionally sent in English. We've resent the message in {lang}, scheduled a live onboarding session for your timezone, and added a $200 credit to help with testing. Reply if you'd like a private walkthrough."
Maya Chen: I'll send localized variants (JP/KR) and attach the office-hours calendar links. Sending to the 8 accounts now at +30m after Jules confirms.
Jules Rivera: Confirmed — ready to run in 30m. I’ll monitor delivery and the outbound logs for language headers. If anything else pops up I’ll post updates here.
Luka (Acme): Thanks team — appreciate the quick turnaround. I'll let my onboarding team know and follow up if anyone still sees English text.
Maya Chen: Thank you, Luka. We'll post a final status update once all 8 resends succeed and will include the RCAs + remediation steps in the follow-up.
Adrian Patel: Postmortem note: we'll add an automated test that asserts Accept-Language is present on outbound onboarding messages. Assigning to eng-infra for next sprint.
Maya Chen: Closing loop — timeline for customers: fix applied in ~15m, resends started at +30m, credits applied immediately. Follow-up survey in 72 hours. I'll draft the customer-facing incident note and share for quick review before broadcasting. :thumbsup:
